pr_title: Cleanup portforward streams after their usage
pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
This implements a stream cleanup when using portforwardings. Before
applying this patch, the streams []httpstream.Stream within
`spdy/connection.go` would fill-up for each streaming request. This
could result in heavy memory usage. Now we use the stream identifier to
keep track of them and finally remove them again once they're no longer
needed.
#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
<!--
*Automatically closes linked issue when PR is merged.
Usage: `Fixes #<issue number>`, or `Fixes (paste link of issue)`.
_If PR is about `failing-tests or flakes`, please post the related issues/tests in a comment and do not use `Fixes`_*
-->
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/100283

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
For testing and CI purposes, I implemented the same change in CRI-O https://github.com/cri-o/cri-o/pull/4625
Nevertheless, I would prefer having the change here.
#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
<!--
If no, just write "NONE" in the release-note block below.
If yes, a release note is required:
Enter your extended release note in the block below. If the PR requires additional action from users switching to the new release, include the string "action required".

For more information on release notes see: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/release-notes.md
-->
```release-note
Fixed port-forward memory leak for long-running and heavily used connections.
```

Please use the following format for linking documentation:

```

/sig node
/cc @haircommander

issue_context.title: Resource/memory leak for long running and reused portforward connections
issue_context.body:
The original problem was discovered with CRI-O, which points to a general solution in k/k proposed in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/99839

### Description

The following example assumes that an nginx web server is running in a POD and that 'crictl port-forward POD_ID 8080:8080' is being used to forward local http requests to the web server.

When CRI-O receives a port forward API request (via stream_port in `/etc/crio/crio.conf`, default `10010`) from clients such as crictl, a TCP connection gets established between CRI-O and the client.

```
                                             TCP connection
                                crictl <-- Host_IP:stream_port --> crio
```

crictl then listens for connection requests on the local address:port (127.0.0.1:8080). When a process such as curl connects to the local address:port, crictl and CRI-O establish a logical `dataStream` and `errorStream` over the TCP connection shown above. CRI-O launches an socat process to establish a connection to the web server on curl's behalf. http requests from curl and responses from the web server can subsequently flow through various connections as shown in this diagram (crictl, CRI-O and socat are acting as intermediaries).

```
                                         .---- dataStream -----.
    curl <-- 127.0.0.1:8080 --> crictl <-                       -> crio <--> socat TCP4:localhost:8080 <--> nginx
                                         '---- errorStream ----'
```

CRI-O creates a dedicated `{dataStream,errorStream}` pair for each invocation of curl. The following diagram shows CRI-O's in-memory data structures that are relevant to the problem at hand.

```
    connection [1]
   .--------------.
.--|- conn        |
|  |              |
|  |  streams[] --|-->.-----.
|  |              |   |   --|--------------------------.
|  '--------------'   |   --|--.                       |
|                     |  :  |  |                       |
|                     '-----'  |                       |
|                              |     Stream [3]        |     Stream [3]
|   Connection [2]             +-->.------------.      +-->.-------------.
'->.--------------.            |   | dataStream |      |   | errorStream |
   |              |            |   '------------'      |   '-------------'
   |  streams[] --|-->.-----.  |                       |
   |              |   |   --|--'                       |
   '--------------'   |   --|--------------------------'
                      |  :  |
                      '-----'
```

[1] type connection struct in vendor/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/httpstream/spdy/connection.go

```
     32 type connection struct {
     33         conn             *spdystream.Connection
     34         streams          []httpstream.Stream
     :
     37 }
```

[2] type Connection struct in vendor/github.com/docker/spdystream/connection.go

```
    176 type Connection struct {
     :
    188         streams    map[spdy.StreamId]*Stream
     :
    205 }
```

[3] type Stream struct in vendor/github.com/docker/spdystream/stream.go

```
     19 type Stream struct {
     20         streamId  spdy.StreamId
     :
     22         conn      *Connection
     :
     38 }
```

The `streams[]` map entries pertaining to `dataStream` and `errorStream` in type Connection struct [2] get cleaned up when the data flow between curl and the web server is complete.

```
  vendor/k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/kubelet/server/portforward/httpstream.go

    238 func (h *httpStreamHandler) portForward(p *httpStreamPair) {
    239         defer p.dataStream.Close()
    240         defer p.errorStream.Close()
     :
    246         err := h.forwarder.PortForward(h.pod, h.uid, int32(port), p.dataStream)
     :
    254 }
```

```
  vendor/github.com/docker/spdystream/stream.go

    155 func (s *Stream) Close() error {
    156         select {
    157         case <-s.closeChan:
    158                 // Stream is now fully closed
    159                 s.conn.removeStream(s)
```

```
  vendor/github.com/docker/spdystream/connection.go

    925 func (s *Connection) removeStream(stream *Stream) {
     :
    927         delete(s.streams, stream.streamId) <------- this removes the map entry
     :
    931 }
```

The problem is that the `streams[]` array entries pertaining to `dataStream` and `errorStream` in type connection struct [1] do _not_ get cleaned up at this stage. These array entries remain until the TCP connection between crictl and CRI-O gets closed, for example, when the crictl process terminates.

```
  vendor/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/httpstream/spdy/connection.go

     78 func (c *connection) Close() error {
     :
     84         c.streams = make([]httpstream.Stream, 0) <- this deallocates the entire array
     :
     91 }
```

Therefore, if the TCP connection between crictl and CRI-O remains open for a long time and if many curl processes are using this connection for port forwarding during that time, then the `streams[]` array in type connection struct [1] can grow massively. This can be demonstrated easily as follows.

#### In terminal window 1

- installed versions of cri-o and cri-tools packages
```
# rpm -q cri-o cri-tools
cri-o-1.11.16-0.4.dev.rhaos3.11.git3f89eba.el7.x86_64
cri-tools-1.11.1-2.rhaos3.11.gitedabfb5.el7.x86_64
```

- restart the cri-o service so that the crio daemon will initially be in a 'clean' state

```
# systemctl restart cri-o
```

- these are the pod and container config files that are needed by crictl and crio to start the nginx container

```

```

CTR=`crictl create $POD ContainerConfig.json PodSandboxConfig.json`

crictl exec $CTR bash -c "nginx"
echo
crictl pods -v
crictl ps -v
runc ps $CTR
echo
```
